texts.facts: These are the two claim petitions bearing no.(s) 207/18 and 208/18 filed by injured Mohd. Faisal and injured Nasir Ahmad. Both the petitions have arisen out of the same accident. The petitioners have filed the claim petitions claiming the compensation under Section 166 & 140 of the Motor Vehicle act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as 'the Act') for the injuries sustained in a road accident that occurred on 13.09.2017 at about 12.30 PM on MH-24 infront of Ganpati Dhaba near Syana Chople Overbridge, within the jurisdiction of police station Garhmukteshwar, Distt. Hapur due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing no. UK-04PA-1153 by the respondent no. 1 which was owned by respondent no. 2. 2. The brief facts as per present petition's are that on 13.09.2017 Nasir Ahmad alongwith his son Mohd. Faisal and three other relatives were going to Shahjanpur, UP from Delhi by a Etios car bearing no. HR-51BB-5516 via NH-24. At about 12.30 PM when they reached infront of Ganpati Dhaba near Syana Chopla Over bridge under PS Garh Muktashwar, District Hapur, UP, an Uttrakhand Roadways bus bearing no. UK-04PA- 1153 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner hit their car bearing no. HR-51BB-5516 from behind due to which all the occupants of the car were critically injured. 3. Notice of the petitions were issued to the respondents. Mohd. Faisal vs. Narender Kumar and Ans. Nasir Ahmad vs. Narender Kumar and Ans. Pursuant to notice, the respondents filed their written statements. 4. The respondent no. 1 in his written statement denied all the allegations and stated that the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident. No cause of action arose in favour of the petitioner and against the respondent no.1. However he admitted that he was working as a driver in the Uttrakhand Roadways and was having a valid driving license which was valid on the date of accident. He further submitted that he has been falsely implicated in the present case. 5. Separate WS also filed on behalf of the the respondent no. 2/ Uttrakhand Roadways resisting the claim on the ground that the accident has taken place due to the negligence of the person who was driving the ETIOS Car bearing no. HR-51 BB- 5516 on NH-24 in a very rash and negligent manner. That the driver of the said car hit the bus bearing no. UK04PA-1153 and the bus was damaged due to the forceful impact of the car. The driver of the bus bearing no. UK-04PA-1153 was driving the bus in a very normal speed and following traffic rules at the time of accident. 6. IN CASE OF NASIR AHMAD MEDICAL EXPENSES : 25. As per the MLC, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries. The petitioner has filed medical bills to the tune of Rs.37,213/-. Medical bills are in the name of petitioner coincide with the period of treatment. In the present case the petitioner has filed original medical bill of Rs. 63,131/-/-. Therefore, I award Rs.63,131/- to the petitioner towards medical expenses. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS AND ENJOYMENT OF LIFE : 34. As per the discharge summary, the petitioner was diagnosed with RTA. In the present case the petitioner has not placed on record any document with regard to special diet, conveyance and attendant charges. However, the injuries on his person were such that he must have taken special diet for his early recovery. He must have spent some amount on conveyance and attendant. Therefore, looking into all the facts, I award Rs.40,000/- to the petitioner towards special diet, conveyance and attendant charges. Loss of Income 36. The petitioner stated that at the time of accident was working with Lite Bite Foods Pvt. Ltd and was earning Rs.14,278/- per month. He has placed on record Joining letter and salary certificate as Ex.PW-1/6. The respondents have not challenged the same by producing any document or examining any witness to this effect. Therefore, an amount of Rs.14,278/- is taken as salary of the petitioner Mohd. Faisal. The injuries on the person of the petitioner were such that he must have remained out of work at least for three months. Thus, the loss of income comes to Rs.42,834/- (Rs.14,278/- x 3). 37. As the offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1 therefore, primary liability to compensate the petitioners is that of respondent no. 1. As the offending vehicle was owned by respondent no. 2 therefore, it becomes vicariously liable to compensate the petitioners. It is an admitted position on record that the offending vehicle was not insured. Therefore, the liability to compensate the petitioners would remain with respondent no.2 i.e. Uttrakhand Transport Corporation Ltd. RELIEF 39. texts.arguments: Counsel for the petitioner has argued forcefully that from the evidence of PWs coupled with the criminal record placed, the petitioner has proved the fact that it was the respondent no. 1 who had caused injuries to the injured persons by his rash and negligent driving. 18. It has been vehemently contended on behalf of the counsel for the respondent no. 2/ Uttrakhand Transport Corporation Ltd. that the accident has occurred due to the negligence of the deceased himself. Both the petitioners PW1 and PW2 had categorically deposed about the manner and occurrence of the accident which was due to rash and negligent driving of the Respondent No.1. No other version of accident has come on record except the one as narrated by injured. The driver of the offending vehicle has never challenged the filing of the chargesheet against him for any false implication. It is pertinent to note that the respondent no. 1/ driver of the offending vehicle Mohd. Faisal vs. Narender Kumar and Ans. Nasir Ahmad vs. Narender Kumar and Ans. was the material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident had taken place. However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box during the course of the inquiry. Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing no. UK-04PA-1153. He has not even cross examined the PWs despite opportunity being given. In his W/S the driver of the offending vehicle Respondent no.1 has stated that his vehicle was not involved in the accident whereas, owner of the vehicle in its WS has not made any such submission. In the WS of respondent no.2 the objection raised in the claim is only that the vehicle bearing no. HR-51BB-5516 driven by the injured was rash and negligent in driving due to which the accident has taken place. This is the basic premise and once that is grasped, it clearly follows that the same injury or loss may affect two different persons in different ways. Take the case of a marginal farmer who does his cultivation work himself and ploughs his land with his own two hands; or the puller of a cycle-rickshaw, one of the main means of transport in hundreds of small towns all over the country. The loss of one of the legs either to the marginal farmer or the cycle- rickshaw-puller would be the end of the road insofar as their earning capacity is concerned. The question of loss of earning capacity resulting from amputation of one the legs in the case of a tanker driver was considered by this Court in K. Janardhan v. United India Insurance Company Limited and another, (2008) 8 SCC 518. In that case, a tanker driver suffered serious injuries in a motor accident and as a result, his right leg was amputated upto the knee joint. He made a claim under the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923. The Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation held that disability suffered by him as a result of the loss of the leg was 100% and awarded compensation to him on that basis. In appeal, the High Court, like in the present case, referred to the Schedule to the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 and held that the loss of a leg on amputation amounted to reduction in the earning capacity by 60% and, accordingly, reduced the compensation awarded to the tanker driver. Ajay Kumar and another, (2011) 1 SCC 343, this Court considered in great detail the correlation between the physical disability suffered in an accident and the loss of earning capacity resulting from it. In paragraphs 10, 11 and 13 of the judgment in Raj Kumar, this Court made the following observations: Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earnings would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity. Ajay Kumar & Anrs., 2011(1) SCC 343 :- Mohd. Faisal vs Narender Kumar And Ans on 28 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60572762/ 10 "Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earnings would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity. In most of the cases, the percentage of economic loss, that is, the Mohd. Faisal vs. Narender Kumar and Ans. percentage of loss of earning capacity, arising from a permanent disability will be different from the percentage of permanent disability. However, in the recent judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case title Pappu Deo Yadav vs. Naresh Kumar and Ors., Civil Appeal No. 2567 of 2020 wherein it was held that future prospects must be considered even in the case of permanent disability.
